Let

\[
S=\left|y_1-y_2\right|+\left|y_2-y_3\right|+\cdots+\left|y_{1992}-y_{1993}\right|.
\]

Set \(n=1993\), and define the consecutive differences

\[
d_i=x_{i+1}-x_i \qquad (i=1,2,\dots,n-1).
\]

The given condition becomes

\[
\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|d_i|=1993=n.
\]

Adding a constant to every \(x_i\) does not change any \(x_i-x_{i+1}\), and it also does not change any \(y_k-y_{k+1}\). So we may assume \(x_1=0\). Then

\[
x_j=d_1+d_2+\cdots+d_{j-1}.
\]

For \(k=1,2,\dots,n-1\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
y_{k+1}-y_k
&=\frac{x_1+\cdots+x_{k+1}}{k+1}-\frac{x_1+\cdots+x_k}{k} \\
&=\frac{kx_{k+1}-(x_1+\cdots+x_k)}{k(k+1)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now

\[
x_{k+1}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}d_i
\]

and

\[
x_1+\cdots+x_k=\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}(k-i)d_i.
\]

Therefore

\[
\begin{aligned}
kx_{k+1}-(x_1+\cdots+x_k)
&=k\sum_{i=1}^{k}d_i-\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}(k-i)d_i\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{k}i d_i.
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence

\[
y_{k+1}-y_k=\frac{1}{k(k+1)}\sum_{i=1}^{k} i d_i.
\]

Using the triangle inequality,

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\left|y_{k+1}-y_k\right|\\
&\le \sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\frac{1}{k(k+1)}\sum_{i=1}^{k} i|d_i|\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1} i|d_i|\sum_{k=i}^{n-1}\frac{1}{k(k+1)}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Now

\[
\frac{1}{k(k+1)}=\frac1k-\frac1{k+1},
\]

so

\[
\sum_{k=i}^{n-1}\frac{1}{k(k+1)}
=\frac1i-\frac1n.
\]

Thus

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&\le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} i|d_i|\left(\frac1i-\frac1n\right)\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|d_i|\left(1-\frac{i}{n}\right).
\end{aligned}
\]

Since \(i\ge 1\), we have \(1-\frac{i}{n}\le 1-\frac1n\). Therefore

\[
S\le \left(1-\frac1n\right)\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|d_i|.
\]

Using \(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}|d_i|=n\),

\[
S\le \left(1-\frac1n\right)n=n-1.
\]

With \(n=1993\),

\[
S\le 1992.
\]

It remains to show that equality is attainable. Take

\[
x_1=0,\qquad x_2=x_3=\cdots=x_{1993}=1993.
\]

Then

\[
|x_1-x_2|+|x_2-x_3|+\cdots+|x_{1992}-x_{1993}|=1993.
\]

Also,

\[
y_k=\frac{x_1+\cdots+x_k}{k}=\frac{1993(k-1)}{k}.
\]

So

\[
\begin{aligned}
S
&=\sum_{k=1}^{1992}\left|y_{k+1}-y_k\right|\\
&=1993\sum_{k=1}^{1992}\frac{1}{k(k+1)}\\
&=1993\left(1-\frac1{1993}\right)\\
&=1992.
\end{aligned}
\]

Therefore the maximum possible value is

\[
\boxed{1992}.
\]
